data.claim: git diff renders a tracked binary as "Binary files ... differ" with no content, so a second edit of an already-modified tracked binary leaves tree_fingerprint unchanged (B95, docs/BACKLOG.md:1142).
data.falsifier: tree_fingerprint returns the same value before and after a same-size second edit of a modified tracked binary.
data.mechanism: Claimed: the digest input is the text of `git diff HEAD`, and that text was assumed to hold nothing about binary content. Actual: git diff prints the header line `index <old>..<new>` for a binary too, and <new> is the blob id git computes from the working copy (diff_fill_oid_info hashes it), so the rendered text changes whenever the bytes do. tree_identity, which gates record since B-uni-tree-identity, names full blob ids and never relied on the diff text.

data.question: Is tree_fingerprint blind to a re-edit of an already-dirty tracked binary file?

data.reason: REFUTED by probe R-B95-binary-reedit (main e234caf3c, git 2.43.0): a same-size second edit of an already-modified tracked binary MOVES tree_fingerprint in all 9 shapes tried (default, staged, new staged, attr binary, attr -diff, same mtime, bigFileThreshold, core.abbrev=4). git diff prints 'index <old>..<new>' for a binary and <new> is the blob id of the working copy, so the digest does see it; tree_identity, what gates record, names full blob ids. No defect to fix. Blocked by the import as THEORETICAL, not by an operator.

data.body: Phase corrections pass. R-B95-binary-reedit REFUTED B95: `git diff` prints `index <old>..<new>` for a binary and <new> is the working copy's blob id, so `tree_fingerprint` moves on a binary re-edit. The docstring of `tree_fingerprint` and docs/BACKLOG.md (B87, B95 and the list at line 95) still state the opposite as a known limit, so a reader trusts a false claim. Change: correct those statements, and add a test that fails if the digest stops seeing the binary re-edit (mutation: drop the `index` line from the digested diff). No behaviour change.

data.body:
Fixes bug B-ci-full-skips-tests-on-events-head: ddflow ci run --full --ref main, when the ref equals the base, scopes the default pre-push command to sha^..sha (_default_on_the_diff, runner.py:228). On main the head is usually an `events:` commit touching only .ddflow/, and the pre-commit `tests` hook has files: ^(ddflow/|tests/|...), so it is Skipped: --full runs no test, exits 0, and api/cirun.py then records cadence.ran integration_tests. Measured: pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push --from-ref e234caf3c --to-ref 4fadc519c with the same files: pattern printed '(no files to check)Skipped'. Expected: --full always runs the whole suite (e.g. --all-files, or the tests hook not diff-filtered). The whole run of ddflow ci run --full was not itself observed on such a head; the skip was measured with a probe hook. Worked around for the 2026-11-05 baseline by passing --base 2773eb435, an ancestor whose diff holds ddflow/ files.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B-ci-full-skips-tests-on-events-head --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B-ci-full-skips-tests-on-events-head --regression-test <test>` first).

Seen again 2026-11-05 by close-blb87 on main f8c6444f5 and 057a4a6b0 (one events-only commit each): `ddflow ci run --full --ref <sha>` printed `ci: passed` with only gitleaks run and `ddflow-ci-scope` scope=full. Workaround that also fails: `--command 'pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push --all-files'` is the default phrase, so `_scope_the_run` silently rewrites it to `--from-ref ... --to-ref HEAD`: an explicit all-files request is narrowed with no notice. The fix should cover that too. Real workaround: pin --ref to the last commit that touched ddflow/ or tests/.
